Here is a cohesive, full 12-week plan summary that integrates all prior requests: phase structure, weekly structure, resistance programming, cardio/aerobic base, HIIT and plyometric components, endometriosis considerations, and the optional 1RM testing discussion. Client snapshot (reference)
- Age/Sex: 34-year-old female
- Condition: Stage III endometriosis
- Cycle: regular cycle ~27 days; last period 2026-05-04
- Flare windows: 2026-07-10 to 07 (flare) and 2026-08-04 to 08-07 (flare)
- Training goals: pain management, functional strength, core/pelvic stability, aerobic base, safe progression within cycle constraints
- Constraints: On flow days and flare days: no HIIT, no heavy Valsalva, no jumping

Overall plan framework
- Duration: 12 weeks, starting 2026-06-01
- Phases:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Base conditioning, technique, low-to-moderate loads, establish breathing and pelvic stability
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Intensification of strength with higher volume on main lifts, tempo work, and introduction of plyometrics and HIIT-informed conditioning
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Peak work capacity with sustained strength, higher cardio tolerance, and maintenance of low-impact constraints during flare windows
- Weekly layout (typical): 3 resistance sessions + 1–2 cardio/conditioning days + 1 optional recovery day
- Core constraints applied each week: no HIIT on flow/flare days; no heavy Valsalva; avoid jumping on flow/flare days

Phase-by-phase detail

Phase 1: Base conditioning and technique (Weeks 1–4)
- Goals: establish mechanics, diaphragmatic breathing, pelvic stability, and foundational strength with light-to-moderate loads. Begin aerobic base building with steady-state cardio.
- Weekly pattern (example):
  - Day 1: Resistance A (full body emphasis)
    - Warm-up: 5–8 minutes light cardio + dynamic mobility
    - Goblet squat: 2–3 x 12
    - Romanian deadlift (RDL): 2–3 x 12
    - Push-up (knees or incline): 2–3 x 10–12
    - Seated row (band): 2–3 x 12
    - Hip thrust (bodyweight/light DB): 2–3 x 12
    - Pallof press: 2–3 x 10 per side
    - Plank: 3 x 20–30 sec
    - Optional: glute bridge 2 x 15
  - Day 2: Cardio + Mobility
    - 20–25 minutes steady-state cardio (elliptical/walk)
    - Mobility circuit focusing on hips, thoracic spine, diaphragmatic breathing
  - Day 3: Resistance C (upper body emphasis)
    - DB floor press or incline press: 3 x 10–12
    - DB row: 3 x 10–12
    - Shoulder lateral raise: 2–3 x 12
    - Band pull-aparts: 2–3 x 12
    - Core: dead bug 3 x 12 per side
    - Side plank: 2 x 20–30 sec per side
  - Day 4: Rest/Active recovery or light mobility
  - Day 5: Optional cardio day or mobility
- Key cues: tempo 2–0–2; diaphragmatic breathing; pelvic floor activation integrated into warm-ups
- Progression: Week 2 adds 1 more set to main lifts; Week 3 includes slight rep increases or tempo refinement; Week 4 deload with lighter loads but preserved technique

Phase 2: Strength intensification, introduce plyometrics and HIIT-informed conditioning, build aerobic base (Weeks 5–8)
- Goals: increase loading on main lifts, add tempo work to drive time under tension, introduce plyometrics cautiously, add a weekly HIIT-informed metabolic conditioning day (low-impact), and expand aerobic conditioning
- Intensity framework: 
  - Main lifts: 3–4 sets, 8–12 reps, RPE ~6–7/10 on non-flare days
  - Tempo: 2-0-2 or 3-1-2; focus on controlled descent/accelerations with reduced intra-abdominal strain
  - Accessory work: 3–4 sets of 10–12 reps, unilateral work included
- Plyometric day (Weeks 5–8):
  - Low-impact plyometrics with emphasis on soft landings and core bracing
  - Week 5: 2–3 sets of 6 x two-foot box or step-down hops (soft landings) or 6 x 10 cm hurdles
  - Week 6: 6 x 8–10 cm box jumps or depth jumps to a box, or 6 x pogo hops
  - Week 7: adjust for flare; swap to plyo-lite or skip and perform balance drills if symptoms arise
  - Week 8: 6 x 12 cm box jumps or 6 x lateral bounds with soft landings
  - Plyo alternatives if jumping is not tolerated: cone taps, quick lateral hops, lateral bound to mat
  - Accessory core: 2–3 sets of 8–12 reps to support plyometrics (e.g., Pallof press, dead bug)
- HIIT/Metabolic Conditioning day (Weeks 5–8; Phase 2):
  - 1 weekly HIIT-inspired day, 10–15 minutes total intervals
  - Modality options: stationary bike, rowing, incline treadmill walk
  - Structure: 6 rounds of 20s high-intensity effort, 40–60s recovery; total work 2–3 minutes, plus warm-up/cool-down

  - Mon: Phase 2 Session A (strength lower/hips emphasis, heavier load)
  - Tue: Cardio base 30 minutes
  - Wed: Phase 2 Session C (upper body emphasis)
  - Thu: Plyometric Day (low-height, emphasis on landing mechanics) or rest if symptomatic
  - Fri: Cardio base 30–40 minutes
  - Sat: Optional HIIT day (metCon) if energy allows and not a flare day
  - Sun: Rest or mobility

- Resistance training:
  - Revisit 3–4 sets for primary lifts, 8–12 reps; maintain tempo and form
  - Some days reduced load during flare windows; on non-flare days, push toward 3–4 x 10–12 with stabilization work
- Plyometric day:
  - Maintain as a maintenance option if tolerated; reduce volume to 1 day per week or switch to plyo-lite if symptoms arise
- HIIT day:
  - Keep as an optional metabolic conditioning day, 1x per week if energy and symptom tolerance permit; otherwise keep to base cardio
- Cardio:
  - Week 9–12: target 30–45 minutes per cardio session; two to three days per week; one longer weekend session if energy allows (up to 45 minutes)
  - Flare days: keep cardio low-intensity, 10–20 minutes, or skip

  - Optional: test 1RM for 2–3 prioritized lifts when symptom-free and with clinician clearance
  - Safer alternative: 3–5RM or submax tests with velocity-based estimation or Brzycki/Epley formulas to project 1RM
  - If test performed: ensure full warm-up, 3–5 minutes rest between attempts, and post-test recovery; drop heavy lifting for 24–48 hours after testing
- Recovery and nutrition:
  - Maintain anti-inflammatory nutrition plan
  - Ensure protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day; adjust carbs around workouts
  - Prioritize sleep 7–9 hours, stress management, mobility work, pelvic floor activation

- Breathing and pelvic floor: continuous diaphragmatic breathing and pelvic floor activation throughout warm-ups and exercises
- Sleep and recovery: target 7–9 hours; include 5–10 minutes daily of diaphragmatic breathing or mindfulness

1RM testing considerations (as previously discussed)
- If testing at end of Phase 3 is desired, schedule on a symptom-minimized, non-flow day (tentatively Week 12)
- Choose 2–3 lifts (squat variation, hip hinge variation, and press variation) with safer options (goblet/front squats, Romanian deadlift or trap-bar deadlift, floor press)

- A one-page printable record for Phase 3 progression and a 1RM testing protocol (including warm-ups, attempts, and safety checks)
